newsitem.title: UK: UK TELECOMS GROUP GRANGER TO LINK UP CHECHNYA.
newsitem.headline: UK TELECOMS GROUP GRANGER TO LINK UP CHECHNYA.

text.p: Granger Telecom, a privately-owned UK telecoms company, said on Wednesday it had won a $300 million contract to design and build a radio-based telecoms network for the Russian breakaway Chechen Republic in the north Caucasus region.

Granger, which was formed in 1993 after a management buyout from its American parent, said work on the five-year project began this week. The first delivery for the Chechen capital Grozny is scheduled for January 1, 1998.

By 2002, more than 95 percent of the Chechen population should be linked up to the most advanced telecoms system in the CIS and will allow Chechnya to embark on rapid commercial development, Granger said.
National operator Chechentelecom said 300,000 lines would link urban and rural areas throughout Chechnya with the outside world using Granger's "CD2000" wireless access system.

The network will need neither underground nor overhead cables and will be able to deliver voice, Internet computer access, high speed ISDN technology (Integrated Services Digital Network), multimedia and high speed data services across wide areas.
